title: 1994–95 Bundesliga - Grokipedia
content: Bundesliga.](#ref-4) The season featured an intensely competitive title race that went down to the wire on the final day, with Dortmund defeating Hamburger SV 2–0 while Bremen drew 0–0 against Bayern Munich, securing the champions' qualification for the 1995–96 UEFA Champions League.](#ref-5) Midfielder Andreas Möller emerged as a pivotal figure for Dortmund, contributing 14 goals and 10 assists in their triumphant campaign under manager Ottmar Hitzfeld.](#ref-5) Offensively, the league saw prolific scoring, highlighted by Mario Basler of Werder Bremen and Heiko Herrlich of Borussia Mönchengladbach sharing the top scorer honor with 20 goals each.](#ref-6)](#ref-7) Freiburg's third-place finish marked a breakthrough for the club, earning them a spot in the UEFA Cup and underscoring the growing competitiveness beyond traditional powerhouses like Bayern Munich, who ended fifth.](#ref-3) The campaign also reflected broader league dynamics, with an average attendance of 30,086 per match across 306 games, maintaining the Bundesliga's reputation for vibrant fan support.](#ref-8) Dynamo Dresden's relegation was particularly poignant, as the club faced financial collapse shortly after, leading to their expulsion from professional football.](#ref-9).
